Subject: Runtime resilience & SDK integration: action items and timeline

Hi Sam —

Great to meet last week. Attaching a brief list of integration requirements and a proposed kickoff agenda (redwood_integration_requirements.pdf). High-level goals: get your SDK consumer-ready, validate endpoint migration, and lock in retry/timeouts and rate-limit behaviour before we flip traffic.

Quick notes for your team before we meet:
- SDKs we ship: Node (npm), Python (pip), and a lightweight Go client. We can share sample snippets for your preferred stack.
- Endpoint migration: we provide a compatibility path — v1 -> v2 proxying for 30 days, then cutover. Plan for a phased ramp (10%, 50%, 100%).
- Retries/timeouts: default client config uses exponential backoff with jitter; recommend timeouts of 15s per token request and an overall request timeout of 60s for long generation calls.
- Rate limits: our hosted API returns X-RateLimit-Limit / X-RateLimit-Remaining / X-RateLimit-Reset headers; for spiky workloads use client-side leaky-bucket smoothing.

Can you confirm your preferred runtime (Node/Python/Go) and whether you need us to pre-generate SDK keys for a sandbox org?

Proposed kickoff window: Tue 6/8 or Wed 6/9 morning PT.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference

Hey Sam — looping in quick technical guidance below (quoting your note). I'm on the engineering handoff for the integration and will join the kickoff.

Quoted: "can you provide sample client code with recommended retry/backoff and an opinionated timeout config?"

Short answer: yes. Two minimal samples (Node and curl) and guidance follows.

Node (recommended client usage):
```js
const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference');
const client = new Redwood.Client({ apiKey: process.env.RW_API_KEY, timeout: 60000 }); // 60s overall

async function generate(prompt) {
  return client.generate({ model: 'redwood/quality-1', input: prompt, retry: { retries: 4, factor: 2, minTimeout: 500, maxTimeout: 8000, jitter: true } });
}
```

curl (single-shot):
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RW_API_KEY" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood/quality-1","input":"hello"}' --max-time 60

Retry & backoff guidance:
- Client-side: exponential backoff with full jitter. Start with min 500ms, cap at 8s, max 4 retries for idempotent requests.
- Server-side 429 handling: respect Retry-After if present. If absent, apply exponential backoff and consult X-RateLimit-Remaining.
- Non-idempotent long-running calls: prefer server-side streaming + checkpointing rather than blind client retries.

Timeouts:
- Token-level timeout: 15s per token chunk (for streaming), overall request timeout: 60s.
- If you expect >60s generation, use our async job endpoint (we return job id + status webhook).

Rate-limiter alignment:
- Map your token-bucket to our X-RateLimit-Limit window. Example: if we allow 300 reqs/min for your tier and you have 3 front-end nodes, set per-node burst to 30 reqs/min and global smoothing to 300 reqs/min.
- Use the headers to opportunistically reduce client concurrency before 429s.

Endpoint migration behavior: 
- During the 30-day proxy window both endpoints accept current tokens. We provide new issuer tokens for the v2 endpoint; you can rotate at any time. We recommend rotating on cutover day (D+30) during a low-traffic window and doing a phased ramp (10/50/100).

I'll paste a short checklist for the kickoff call so we can land concrete owners.

Aditya
Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
aditya_rao@redwood.com
